# Secrets and keys

OpenBao holds each site's secrets and keys, and the site's internal certificate authority that cert-manager issues from. Where the site has a hardware security module (HSM), OpenBao is sealed with a key held in it, through the kms-pkcs11 plugin. SoftHSM2 is a software stand-in used only in the lab and in tests.

Back to the [component catalogue](./index.md).

## image:quay.io/openbao/openbao-ubi

**What it provides.** Base of our OpenBao image (OpenBao 2.7.3 on UBI), which adds the pinned kms-pkcs11 plugin.

**Why it is needed.** The OpenBao server, on UBI 9, that our OpenBao image extends with the kms-pkcs11 plugin. OpenBao holds each site's secrets, the internal certificate authority and each person's keys. Without it the site would need another secrets manager; HashiCorp Vault is excluded (D-04).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | Container image |
| Pinned version or digest | `2.7.3@sha256:bb94f6b1f1a3fbb7538d17d1c0509a13f1c2b382ebc1a67b99286b12c9628f71` |
| Architecture component | `openbao` |
| Used in | `deploy/images/openbao/Containerfile` |
| Scope | Runtime: it runs in the product |
| Licence | MPL-2.0 (OpenBao); Red Hat UBI EULA (base) |
| Cryptography | Not a validated cryptographic module |
| Air gap | Works with no internet access |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | SC-12, SC-13, SC-28, IA-5, AU-2, AU-9, CP-9 |
| Security fixes | The rebuilt image is scanned by grype (report-only, --only-fixed --fail-on high) in deploy-images on every PR that changes it; the base digest is re-pinned by hand in a reviewed change when Red Hat publishes a fixed image. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- Seal keys are held in a validated site HSM through the kms-pkcs11 plugin, or by Shamir shares under the key ceremony.
- The kms-pkcs11 plugin is v0.3.0, young, and tested on SoftHSM2 only; Shamir is the fallback.
- The audit device is shipped to the site log store; tamper-evidence of the audit log is gap G2 and still open.
- Never HashiCorp Vault (D-04).
- UBI 9 base: its RHEL OpenSSL FIPS provider is the validated-module path only on a host in FIPS mode; the CMVP certificate number for this image is not yet confirmed (Phase 48).
- Built only into images this repository rebuilds (deploy/images, D-23): each is signed with your organization's one cosign key in the container-release environment, with a CycloneDX SBOM and an attestation; no keyless signing.

## image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi

**What it provides.** Build stage of the SoftHSM2 library for the test-only openbao-softhsm image.

**Why it is needed.** Build stage of the test-only image that adds SoftHSM2 to OpenBao, so the lab and CI can test HSM sealing without a hardware HSM. It never reaches production.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | Container image |
| Pinned version or digest | `9.9@sha256:5a8bf48617eb65228e6ed828995ad896492915918632ccce7233a840a5aba664` |
| Architecture component | `hsm` |
| Used in | `deploy/images/openbao-softhsm/Containerfile` |
| Scope | Test only: not shipped |
| Licence | Red Hat UBI EULA (redistributable) |
| Cryptography | None |
| Air gap | Works air-gapped once mirrored: the pinned digest on the connected build host; the site never pulls it (it reaches the site inside our signed image) |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | SC-12, SC-13 |
| Security fixes | The rebuilt image is scanned by grype (report-only, --only-fixed --fail-on high) in deploy-images on every PR that changes it; the base digest is re-pinned by hand in a reviewed change when Red Hat publishes a fixed image. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- SoftHSM2 is test scope only and never appears in production values (D-38).
- The site HSM must hold a FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certificate and run in its approved mode.
- HSM hardware is export-controlled: it follows your organization's Controlled Goods and ITAR procedures.
- Build stage of a test-only image; never in production values.

## chart:openbao

**What it provides.** OpenBao Helm chart 0.30.8, rendered with our rebuilt OpenBao image.

**Why it is needed.** Installs OpenBao, with our rebuilt OpenBao image at the site from the vendored, hash-checked chart tarball, with our settings. Its images come from the pinned image lock. Without the chart we would write and maintain the Kubernetes manifests ourselves.

| Air gap | Works with no internet access |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | SC-12, SC-13, SC-28, IA-5, AU-2, AU-9, CP-9 |
| Security fixes | Bumped by hand in a reviewed change: download the new tarball, check its index SHA-256, update the lock and re-run the render invariants. The chart holds templates only; fixes in the software arrive through its image pins. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- Seal keys are held in a validated site HSM through the kms-pkcs11 plugin, or by Shamir shares under the key ceremony.
- The kms-pkcs11 plugin is v0.3.0, young, and tested on SoftHSM2 only; Shamir is the fallback.
- The audit device is shipped to the site log store; tamper-evidence of the audit log is gap G2 and still open.
- Never HashiCorp Vault (D-04).
- Raft snapshots run on a schedule by a job whose token reads only sys/storage/raft/snapshot, onto an encrypted volume; a snapshot restores only with the HSM or the Shamir shares (47-24).

## tool:kms-pkcs11

**What it provides.** OpenBao kms-pkcs11 plugin 0.3.0: seals OpenBao with a key held in the site HSM.

**Why it is needed.** OpenBao plugin that seals OpenBao with a key held in the site HSM, so the key that unlocks OpenBao never sits on disk. Shamir key shares are the fallback.

**Why it is needed.** A software HSM built into the test-only OpenBao image, so the lab and CI can test HSM sealing without hardware. It never reaches production.
